name: Elzaphan
title: Levitical leader during the wilderness journey
summary: Elzaphan (also known as Elizaphan) was the son of Uzziel, who was the son of Kohath from the tribe of Levi. He was appointed by Moses as leader of the families of the Kohathites and played a role in several important events during Israel's wilderness journey, including in connection with the deaths of Nadab and Abihu.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as leader of the Kohathites
keyEvents.description: Elzaphan, son of Uzziel, was appointed by Moses as leader of the Kohathite clans, with responsibility for the ark of the covenant, the table, the lampstand, the altars, and the holy utensils.

keyEvents.title: Tasks of the Kohathites in the tabernacle
keyEvents.description: As leader of the Kohathites, Elzaphan and his clan were responsible for carrying the most holy items of the tabernacle during Israel's journey through the wilderness.

keyEvents.title: Carrying the Bodies of Nadab and Abihu
keyEvents.description: After Nadab and Abihu died in the Lord's presence because they offered unauthorized fire, Moses commanded Elzaphan and his brother Mishael to carry their bodies out of the sanctuary and away from the camp.

keyEvents.title: The Kohathites Counted in the Census
keyEvents.description: Elzaphan's clan was counted among the Kohathites when Moses and Aaron numbered the Levites by the Lord's command, recording the number of men one month old and upward.

keyEvents.title: Elzaphan's Descendants in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Elzaphan's descendants are mentioned in Chronicles as participants in the service during King David's time and King Hezekiah's religious reforms, when they helped cleanse the temple.
